analysis.title: GS Flow of Funds: Chopsgiving
key_insights: Flows are bifurcated: retail and corporates are buying while institutions sell tech and cut leverage, which keeps net weekly and monthly flow totals tame despite violent day-to-day reversals. The desk calls it a trader's market.

The desk expects equities to grind moderately higher with bumps. The next two weeks still carry turbulence risk, but systematic flows lean to the upside for the first time in weeks and institutional positioning is light.

On the GS prime book, Info Tech was the most net sold global and US sector for another week. The US Info Tech long/short ratio is 1.5 versus a YTD peak of 2.14 in early June, the lowest on record (since 2016).
US Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 1.6 pts to 209.1% (34th percentile, one-year). Net leverage rose 2.1 pts to 45.4% (4th percentile, one-year).

US-listed ETF shorts fell 8.6%, the largest covering in 7 months, led by Large Cap Equity, Credit and Tech ETFs. Single stocks were heavily net sold again (-1.7 SDs, 1-year), driven mainly by short sales.

US-listed equity ETFs took in $59.3bn last week versus $55.2bn the prior week, beating 91% of the 46 weeks this year (weekly average $26.5bn). Fixed income ETF inflows fell to $2.6bn from $13.7bn, with net outflows Thursday and Friday after the hotter-than-expected CPI print.
Semis ETFs lost $7.3bn last week against an average weekly inflow of $6.2bn over the prior four weeks. They lost $5.6bn on Monday alone and saw outflows on each of the last three days.

Levered semis ETF flows swung sharply: SOXL took in $5.10bn in the Nov 5 week (second-largest weekly inflow in a year) then lost $4.17bn the next week (largest weekly outflow in a year). SOXS had $4.38bn of outflows over two weeks and cut its share count by two-thirds. The desk reads this as a lack of conviction.

Global equity funds had net inflows of $98bn in the week ending November 11 versus $89bn the week before. Foreign flows have returned to the US, lifting the 4-week moving average by about $5bn. Money market fund assets fell $18bn.

Retail net bought $6.19bn of US equities last week, the largest weekly total of the 11 weeks since Sep 1. Buying was concentrated in semis and mega-cap tech, led by Nvidia (+$1.75bn), AMD (+$672mm), Micron (+$526mm) and Tesla (+$523mm). The desk says losing retail support could change the setup for US equities into year-end.

Corporate buyback desk volumes are 1.3x 2025 YTD ADTV. About 94% of the S&P 500 is in an open window, rising to about 95% by end of week, and the window is expected to stay open until December 13. 2026 YTD repurchase authorizations are $1.52T versus $1.27T in 2025 YTD.

CTAs sold over $22bn of S&P last week and about $2.5bn of Nasdaq, leaving US equity positioning near -$10bn short, the lowest since April. With vol down from its highs and spot rebounding, CTAs are projected to buy almost $10bn of US equities over the next week in a flat tape.

Vol control and risk parity funds sold over $30bn combined last week. Stocks and bonds fell together after CPI, which typically makes risk parity cut exposure, though the desk expects gradual flows. Vol control may re-risk in December/January if markets calm.

The GS Panic Index is 6.3/10, the 67th percentile on a 1y lookback. VIX volatility and SPX skew rose from the 12th and 38th percentiles on Nov 11 to the 59th and 67th. The desk's vol forecast points to elevated volatility and choppy near-term conditions.
Liquidity is expected to thin into the holidays. Top of book liquidity has stayed robust but is starting to trend lower.

Seasonality: in the 17 years since 1990 when VIX started mid-November at 18 or higher, it was lower by year-end in 14, by 3.25 pts on average. SPX year-end gain in those years averaged +1.34% (up in 59% of years), with a median drawdown of -3.0% inside the window. From Dec 15 to year-end the mean is +1.22% and SPX rose in 27 of 36 years.

sector_views.rationale: Institutions were the heaviest net sellers of Info Tech on the prime book, with the US long/short ratio at a record low of 1.5, while retail bought semis and mega-cap tech. The desk gives no rating.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The print drove fixed income ETF outflows on Thursday and Friday and pushed stocks and bonds lower together, which typically makes risk parity funds cut exposure.

risk_factors: Retail buying could fade or disappoint this week. The desk says losing that support could change the setup for US equities into year-end.
Concerns about AI and broader tech spending, including a recent idiosyncratic episode, are cracking institutional conviction in tech.
CTA flow skew can reverse quickly. Projected one-month flows in a down tape are sellers of $122.97B.
Stocks and bonds falling together after the hot CPI print can force risk parity de-risking.
The next two weeks still pose seasonal turbulence.
vol_and_positioning: GS Panic Index is 6.3/10, the 67th percentile on a 1y lookback. It combines 1-month S&P implied vol, VIX volatility, 1-month put-call skew and the 1m vs 3m term structure slope.
VIX volatility moved from the 12th to the 59th percentile and SPX skew from the 38th to the 67th between Nov 11 and Nov 13 on a rolling 2y lookback.

CTA positioning in US equities is short almost $10bn, the lowest since April. One-week flows are projected as: flat tape buyers $22.97B ($9.86B US), up tape buyers $30.78B ($16.1B US), down tape sellers $6.07B ($5.23B US).
One-month CTA projections: flat tape buyers $13.87B ($8.01B US), up tape buyers $89.1B ($54.04B US), down tape sellers $122.97B ($20.31B US).
Vol control and risk parity sold over $30bn combined last week. Vol control may re-risk in December/January if the market calms.
US Fundamental L/S net leverage is 45.4%, the 4th percentile one-year. Gross leverage is 209.1%, the 34th percentile.
The US Info Tech long/short ratio is 1.5, the lowest on GS record since 2016.

tension_points.bull_case: Retail net bought $6.19bn, corporate buyback windows are about 94% open, CTAs are projected to buy almost $10bn of US equities in a flat tape, and foreign flows are returning to the US. Light institutional positioning makes a sustained move lower hard without going higher first.
tension_points.bear_case: Institutions are net selling tech and cutting leverage, vol control and risk parity sold over $30bn, and the CTA skew can reverse quickly. The next two weeks still carry seasonal turbulence and liquidity thins into the holidays.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Retail buying disappointing or fading this week, which the desk says could drastically change the setup for US equities into year-end.

theme_stances.key_argument: Retail and corporate buyers have defended the market while institutions sold, and losing retail support could drastically change the year-end setup.
theme_stances.evidence: Retail has buoyed the market once again as the AI trade is tested.
